chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Did any of your forefathers ever fast in Sha'ban?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The best of my forefathers, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), fasted it.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

As for what has come regarding the fasting of Sha'ban, he (peace be upon him) was asked about it, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast it, nor did any of my forefathers (peace be upon them).'

He said that because a group said: 'Fasting it is obligatory, like the fasting of the month of Ramadan, and its obligation is like the obligation of the month of Ramadan, and whoever breaks a day from it, upon him is expiation like what is upon the one who breaks a day from the month of Ramadan.'

And the words of the Scholar (peace be upon him): 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast it, nor did any of my forefathers (peace be upon them)' means: 'They did not fast it as an obligatory obligation,' contradicting the words of the one who claimed it is obligatory. And rather, they used to fast it as a Sunnah with virtue, and there is nothing upon the one who does not fast it.

key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)

ai.seo_question: Is fasting in Sha'ban obligatory or recommended in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of fasting in Sha'ban by distinguishing between the Prophet's voluntary practice and the Imams' avoidance of it to refute the claim that it is an obligatory duty (fard) equal to Ramadan. The scholars explain that the Imams did not fast it as a mandatory obligation, thereby correcting the misconception that breaking a fast in Sha'ban incurs the same expiation as Ramadan, while affirming its status as a highly recommended Sunnah.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Did anyone from your<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> Fast during Shaban at all?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The best of my<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> Fasted it’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it.

So, as for what has come regarding the Fasts of Shaban, he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not Fast it, nor did anyone from my<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is because a group was saying that Fasting in it is Obligatory like the Fasts of the Month of Ramazan, and its Obligation is like the Obligation of the Month of Ramazan, and that the one who breaks a day from it, so upon him would be the expiation similar to what it would be upon the one who breaks one day from the Month of Ramazan’.

And rather, the words of the Scholar<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not Fast it, nor did anyone from my<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>’, yes, he<sup>saww</sup> did not Fast it as an Obligated Obligation, in belying the words of the one who alleged that it is an Obligation. And rather, Fasting it is a Sunnah wherein is virtue, and there is not upon the one who does not Fast it, anything’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Safwan from ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“Once, I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Had any of your ancestors ever fasted during the month of Sha‘ban?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘The best of my ancestors, the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, fasted in it.’”
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.

There are narrations about fasting in the month of al-Sha‘ban. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about it and he (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, did not fast (during the month of Sha‘ban) neither did any of my ancestors.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because certain people said that fasting in the month of al-Sha‘ban is obligatory like fasting in the month of Ramadan. If one destroys one day of fasting of month of al-Sha‘ban, the expiation for it is like the expiation for destroying one day of fasting of the month of Ramadan.

The words of the scholar, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘The Messenger of Allah did not fast neither did any of my ancestors’ means they did not fast it as an obligatory fast. It was to refute what certain people thought it to be. Their fast was only as Sunnah in which there is virtue but it is not harmful to one who does not fast.
